idappaccaya:
[(1)idaṃ+paccaya]  CL=7 This specific condition (idappaccaya) is for old age and death (jarāmaraṇa). (2) (A) This condition. (B) A condition where perception arises together with samādhi and arahattaphala.
See - idaṃ.
(2) Ima+paccaya. Ma changes to da. (According to Moga,3.55, Ima changes to idaṃ.Ayameva paccayo idappaccayo, makārassa dakāraṃ katvā. Dakārenapi pakatipadamicchanti keci saddavidū. Sī,ṭī,saca,2.384-5]
idappaccayatā: [Idappaccaya+tā]  CL=7 (1) The condition for this old age and death (jarāmaraṇa) is the dhamma such as birth (jāti), etc., as explained in the sequence of dependent origination (paṭiccasamuppāda): birth (jāti) is the condition for old age and death, existence (bhava) is the condition for birth, clinging (upādāna) is the condition for existence, and ignorance (avijjā) is the condition for volitional formations (saṅkhāra). (2) (A) A collection of interdependent dhammas such as birth (jāti), etc., that constitute the conditions for old age and death (jarāmaraṇa) within the framework of dependent origination (paṭiccasamuppāda). (3) (A) The dependent origination dhamma (paṭiccasamuppāda) explains how birth (jāti), as a condition, gives rise to old age and death (jarāmaraṇa), etc. See - idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppanna. (B) The causal efficacy of ignorance (avijjā), as the root condition, gives rise to volitional formations (saṅkhāra) and subsequently leads to the unfolding of the dependent origination process. See - idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppāda.

idaṃ: [Sabbanāmapuda]  CL=9 Saddanīti mentions that it is not a sabbanāma/pronoun word "ima" among 27 words, but it is the sabbanāma word "ida (idaṃ)" and "ima" is changed from that "ida". See Nīti,sutta.305,307  Kaccāyane tu "imassidamaṃsisu napuṃsake"ti imasaddoyeva pakatibhāvena vutto, idha pana idaṃ(ida¿)saddoyeva, "idappaccayatā"ti ettha "ida"nti pakatiyā dassanato. Nīti,pada.367. Also in the present version of that Saddanīti, the word is found as "idaṃ" as its original form with the niggahita without the case-ending being added such as "idaṃsaddo, idaṃsaddassa", etc. However, in its Nisya versions, it is found as "idasaddo", etc. with the vowel ending. Although there are different readings thus, the original form should be "ida" with the vowel ending according to Saddanīti because it is included in vowel ending in Nīti, sutta. 639. According to Padarūpasiddhi, its original form should be "idaṃ" with the consonantal ending because it is put in consonantal ending like the word "kiṃ" by the word "ca" of the Sutta "pakati cassa sarantassa" of Padarūpasiddhi.  In Pakati cassasarantassasuta in Suttaniddesa, it is said that "idappaccayatāti etaṃ rūpasiddhi ādīsu idaṃsaddo niggahītantoti gahetvā byañjanantassa pakatibhāvenagahitaṃ, saddanīti ādīsu panaidasaddo sarantotigahetvā sarantassa pakatibhāvenagahitaṃ""] this man, this woman, this lineage, this consciousness, this thing, (etc.) See also ima.   idaṃ (bya/indeclinable)It is just an indeclinable particle with no particular meaning and is put just for the euphony of words.

iddhipāda: [Iddhi+pāda]  CL=7 Iddhipāda: (A) A collection of dhammas that constitute the basis for success consisting of chanda (desire), viriya (effort), citta (consciousness), and vīmaṃsā (investigation). (B) (B) The fundamental principles that serve as the basis for the progress and development of living beings. (C) A collection of the four nāma-khanda dhammas (mental aggregates), specifically the remaining citta-cetasika dhammas that function as the basis or foundation for chanda, samādhi, and padhānasaṅkhāra dhammas. (C) These dhammas are associated with the causes of human progress and development, such as wholesome mental states including upacāra jhāna (access concentration).
